title: The Agent That Created 107 PRs (And Why That Was the Problem)
audience: Engineering leaders, DevSecOps practitioners, and senior engineers evaluating AI agents in CI/CD pipelines
tone: Honest and reflective — a real story told without spin, inviting debate and shared experience
key_thesis: An AI agent that acts without analyzing is just a faster way to make mistakes at scale. The missing step between detect and fix is: understand.

sections.heading: The Setup: 107 Pull Requests Waiting for You on Monday Morning
sections.intent: Open with the scene. Engineers arrive to find 107 PRs created overnight by an agent tasked with fixing code scanning alerts. Set the tone — this is not a horror story, but it is a lesson.

sections.heading: What the Agent Did Right
sections.intent: Give the agent credit. It found every alert. It produced a fix for every alert. It moved fast. This section is important — we are not anti-AI, and we need to be fair.

sections.heading: What the Agent Missed: The Analysis Step
sections.intent: The agent treated every alert as a mechanical patch. It never asked: is this the right fix? Is this alert a false positive? Does this change break the intent of the code? The missing step was deliberate reasoning before action.

sections.heading: The Real Cost: Review Burden at Scale
sections.intent: 107 PRs is not a productivity win if each PR requires a human to understand the context, verify the fix is safe, and approve. The agent moved the bottleneck, it did not remove it. In some cases it made it worse.

sections.heading: The Fix: Require a Spec Before the Code
sections.intent: The Spec2PR approach as the antidote. Before the agent writes any code, require it to produce a plan: what alert, what is the root cause, what is the proposed fix, what is the risk of the fix. A human reviews the spec, not 107 PRs.

sections.heading: Let's Talk: Have You Seen This?
sections.intent: Open, conversational closing. Invite readers to share their own experiences. Pose 3-4 direct questions: How do you validate AI agent output? What is your human-AI handoff model? Should agents always require approval of the approach first?
